source: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record - Cholera in 1990 (WER 66(19):133-136)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1990-01-01..1990-12-31. Source states: 'In Africa, 37 960 cases were notified by 10 countries in 1990, compared with 35 951 cases reported by 16 countries in 1989.'. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. Namibia does not appear anywhere in the WER 1990 annual cholera notification table; the Africa block runs ...Malawi / Mali / Mauritania / Mozambique -> Niger / Nigeria... with no Namibia line. Namibia became independent on 1990-03-21 and joined WHO on 1990-04-23; cholera was one of three diseases subject to mandatory notification to WHO under the International Health Regulations (1969) throughout this period, so non-appearance in the annual notification table means no cholera cases were notified, not that no notification channel existed. Corroboration: (a) WHO Global Health Observatory annual cholera series (CHOLERA_0000000001) holds NO Namibia record before 2005 while neighbours are present from 1971 (Angola), 1973 (South Africa, Mozambique, Zimbabwe) and 1978 (Zambia); (b) the peer-reviewed report of Namibia's 2006-2007 outbreak states 'To date, there has been no published data of cholera occurring in Namibia' and 'this is the first published report of cholera from Namibia'. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence - inferred from absence of any notification in a mandatory WHO notification regime, not from an explicit WHO statement that Namibia reported zero. Caveat recorded in the WER 1990 issue itself: 'Evidence was again received of the presence of cholera in a number of other countries which failed to declare it' - underreporting cannot be excluded. Surveillance system status: operational (IHR(1969) cholera notification in force; Namibia a WHO Member State). National-level row; no sub-national rows exist for this period.
